answer_text: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller version of the same problem until it hits a base case simple enough to answer directly — like `factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1)` stopping at `factorial(0) = 1` — with each call sitting on the call stack until the base case unwinds the chain back up into a final answer; without a base case the calls never stop and the stack eventually overflows, but done well recursion reads cleanly on naturally recursive structures like trees.
